note: Existing-source, strict-license-screened public gallery. Additional historical photos remain held from this site. Anatomy overlays are teaching annotations, not a separate verified voucher determination.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — LARGE ONE-SIDED SPIKELETS
tiles.details: Start with species panel 2 (index 1): it really shows the ascending flowering branches and attached ovoid spikelets. UT describes a terminal panicle 80–160+ mm long with at least four principal branches; Kew describes 3–10 racemes. These are published measurements, NOT lengths measured from the unscaled photo. Single or paired spikelets can occur at a node when one partner aborts.
tiles.short: Several ascending panicle branches with conspicuously plump, 4.5–5.9 mm ripe spikelets.
tiles.status: REAL ARCHIVED HEAD PHOTO — LENGTH REQUIRES SCALE

tiles.heading: 02 · ROOTS AND TRUE COLLAR
tiles.details: Follow a source-confirmed U. texana flowering stem to its rooted annual base; lower trailing nodes may root. At the INSIDE blade/sheath junction, distinguish the true truncate 1–1.8 mm ciliate membrane (UT; Kew 1–1.5 mm) from the adjacent white hairy collar (~1.5–2 mm); auricles absent in the UT description. NONE of the existing seven teaching panels actually photographs the opened TRUE inner ligule or a connected rooted flowering base. Formerly linked panel 1 (index 0) is a wide habit view only, not collar/root proof. Collect a source-identified 1-mm-scaled collar photograph.
tiles.short: Fibrous-rooted annual; 1–1.8 mm CILIATE MEMBRANOUS ligule, not merely collar hairs.

tiles.heading: 03 · MEASURE MATURE SPIKELETS AND GLUMES
tiles.details: Use real USDA species panel 3 (index 2) for ventral/dorsal views with printed 1-mm ticks. UT reports lower glume (3)5–7-veined, reaching roughly the middle to two-thirds of the spikelet, and upper glume 5–7-veined and nearly full-length. The 322-pixel plate supports gross orientation/scale, not an invented fine vein-count arrow; take a sharper 10–20× dissection to confirm veins.
tiles.short: Spikelet 4.5–5.9 mm; lower glume 2.4–3.2 mm, upper 4.5–5.6 mm.
tiles.status: ACTUAL ARCHIVED SCALED SPIKELET PLATE — HIGH-RES VEINS STILL MISSING

tiles.heading: 04 · TWO FLORETS; LEMMA, PALEA AND AWN
tiles.details: UT describes the lower floret's ~5-mm membranous five-veined lemma with conspicuous cross-veins and ~4-mm palea. Upper bisexual floret has a tough ~3.5 × 2.2-mm three-veined lemma and ~3.2-mm palea; Kew reports a rugose hardened fertile lemma with an apiculate tip, not a projecting long awn. USDA panel 4 (index 3) shows real fertile florets A/B and caryopses C/D; it does NOT show a leaf ligule or separately spread lower-floret lemma.
tiles.short: Lower staminate floret; upper fertile lemma ~3.5 mm, hardened, cross-ridged, without a long awn.
tiles.status: REAL USDA FERTILE FLORET PHOTO — LOWER-FLORET DISSECTION GAP

tiles.heading: 05 · CENTRAL TEXAS SIGNALGRASS LOOK-ALIKES
tiles.details: Texas U. texana: 4.5–5.9 mm, lower glume ~1/2–2/3; brownseed U. fusca: ~2.4–3.4 mm, lower glume ~1/4–1/3; creeping U. reptans: ~1.5–2.2 mm, lower glume ~1/8–1/4. Panels 5–7 (indices 4–6) are DIFFERENT-species photos; the previous panel 2 (index 1) was U. texana itself and belongs in the LOOK HERE FIRST lesson, not the look-alike-only photo selection. Southern crabgrass Digitaria ciliaris can have fingerlike racemes but a membranous rather than ciliate-membranous ligule; confirm under magnification. Unmeasured immature plants remain Urochloa sp.
tiles.short: Compare ripe spikelet LENGTH and lower-glume fraction, not just seedhead shape.
tiles.status: REAL COMPARISON PHOTOS — MATCHED MILLIMETER SERIES MISSING

tiles.heading: 06 · PUBLIC-READY GATE AND OWNER HANDOFF
tiles.details: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO (Grass Diagnostic Photos / Lane 1): (a) one authenticated Hays-area same-plant rooted annual base, lower rooting node and mature panicle; (b) opened TRUE 1–1.8 mm ciliate membrane with distinct hairy collar/sheath and 1-mm ruler; (c) optional higher-resolution, same-specimen glume-vein and lower cross-veined lemma macro if fine vein counts are to be illustrated, not another ordinary spikelet shot (real USDA mm-scaled glume/floret plates ALREADY exist); (d) matched mature U. fusca/U. reptans ripe spikelets at identical scale. NEEDS_SITE_QA (Grass Public Readiness): verify four real JPEGs, seven gallery panels, thirteen existing gross arrows, Sam Kieschnick CC BY 4.0 and USDA Julia Scher/public-domain credits, correct labels and mobile learner rendering. Clemson and USF photos are research-only without public reuse clearance. Do not change county nativity or claim FINISHED.
tiles.short: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS — 4 local JPEGs and USDA anatomy, not a fully documented Hays specimen.

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: TEXAS SIGNALGRASS: the new close-up now shows multiple ASCENDING branches lined with comparatively large elongate green spikelets (about 4.5–5.9 mm in UT records). On a separately collected ripe spikelet, lower glume typically reaches about HALF to TWO-THIRDS of spikelet length. Don't turn a CC-licensed photo or wide grass clump into confirmed glume lengths without a ruler. TEXAS SIGNALGRASS SECOND DIAGNOSTIC PASS: once a whole head and its large one-sided ascending branches are recognized, confirm on the SAME plant: a 1–1.8 mm membranous ligule with ciliate fringe at opened collar, actual ~4.5–5.9 mm mature spikelets, and lower glume ~2.4–3.2 mm (roughly half to two-thirds of total spikelet). A paired spikelet may be missing because one sibling aborts. Lift both glumes and separate the lower staminate floret from the upper bisexual hard ridged lemma under a 10–20× hand lens. These are field measurements from UT treatment, NOT visible/scaled claims for gallery pixels.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: PHOTO WALK: display all four physically archived Texas signalgrass views first—general habitat, actual Sam Kieschnick panicle, USDA front/back spikelets with mm ticks, then USDA fertile florets and grains. Only AFTER these use the DIFFERENT-SPECIES U. fusca and U. reptans comparison panels.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Follow a source-confirmed U. texana flowering stem to its rooted annual base; lower trailing nodes may root. At the INSIDE blade/sheath junction, distinguish the true truncate 1–1.8 mm ciliate membrane (UT; Kew 1–1.5 mm) from the adjacent white hairy collar (~1.5–2 mm); auricles absent in the UT description. NONE of the existing seven teaching panels actually photographs the opened TRUE inner ligule or a connected rooted flowering base. Formerly linked panel 1 (index 0) is a wide habit view only, not collar/root proof. Collect a source-identified 1-mm-scaled collar photograph.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Start with species panel 2 (index 1): it really shows the ascending flowering branches and attached ovoid spikelets. UT describes a terminal panicle 80–160+ mm long with at least four principal branches; Kew describes 3–10 racemes. These are published measurements, NOT lengths measured from the unscaled photo. Single or paired spikelets can occur at a node when one partner aborts.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: The new Commons panicle photo reveals the real, larger green units; compare with smaller U. fusca (~2.4–3.4 mm, lower glume ~1/4–1/3) and small U. reptans (~1.5–2.2 mm, lower glume ~1/8–1/4). Texas signalgrass has an alternate-branch panicle and a short membranous, ciliate ligule, but the close-up shows no exposed collar or dissected floret.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

memory_rule: U. reptans tiny ~1.5–2.2 mm and minute basal glume; U. fusca blunt ~2.4–3.4 mm with shorter glume; U. texana much larger ~4.5–5.9 mm with lower glume about half/two-thirds.
safety_note: Source IDs and credited Commons photos do not establish county occurrence. Original gross arrows retained; glume/ligule microanatomy is NOT annotated in those images. Correction in detailed pass: Kew documents a 1–1.5mm ciliate membrane; UT Williamson plant description gives 1–1.8mm membranous BASE with fringe and white densely hairy COLLAR. Some broad keys summarize as 'ligule of hairs' but actual collar membrane must be photographed and labeled separately, not assumed identical to collar hairs. Lane 1 check: all four local source JPEGs verified; the two USDA plates are actual locally stored structures with source-marked mm scale. The remaining true ligule and connected Hays rooting-node view have no species-certified archived macro. All current look-alike panels now use independently licensed non-NC photographs. The public Learner still requires mobile/PAGES QA.
field_rule: Rank photos by what they truly show: flowering branch/shape first, followed by mature spikelet length and lower glume measured under 10–20×. Do not treat unmeasured photogenic heads as proof of native versus introduced species.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
